## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with `Spinner` + `SetSpinnerFrame` for a view's own loading, with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`) for work the router tracks. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

# Most tasks are a single `go ...` invocation and run unchanged under both the
# POSIX shell and the "cmd /c" that mise defaults to on Windows. Tasks relying on
# POSIX syntax declare `shell = "bash -c"` explicitly — the global
# `windows_default_inline_shell_args` setting is refused from a project config.

[tools]
go = "1.27"
# Pinned so CI and every machine lint against the same rules. Without a pin, two
# golangci-lint versions disagree on what Rule 305 considers a clean run.
# 2.15.0 is the first line built with Go 1.27 (2.12.2 was built with go1.26 and
# refuses a go.mod that targets 1.27: "Go language version used to build
# golangci-lint is lower than the targeted Go version").
golangci-lint = "2.15.0"
# Pinned for the same reason, and it matters more here: goreleaser's own
# configuration schema changes between minor versions, so an unpinned tool
# would fail on `version: 2` syntax that was valid when it was written.
goreleaser = "2.18.0"
# Pinned for the same reason as the two above. Used by docs-serve/docs-build
# to run mkdocs-material without installing it as a mise tool: mkdocs-material
# is a theme/plugin package, not an app — it exposes no console-script entry
# point of its own (only its dependency `mkdocs` does), so `pipx:mkdocs-material`
# fails on every platform with "No executables are provided by package
# `mkdocs-material`". `uv tool run --with` sidesteps this by running `mkdocs`
# (which has an entry point) in an ephemeral environment with mkdocs-material
# injected alongside it.
uv = "0.12.10"

[tasks.build]
description = "Build the binary to bin/dk"
# `$(go env GOEXE)` for the same reason as [tasks.install]: `-o` takes the name
# literally, and PowerShell refuses to run an extension-less file even by
# explicit path — "Cannot run a document in the middle of a pipeline". Only
# `mise run run` uses this binary today, and it goes through bash, which is why
# nothing has complained. Empty on every other platform.
#
# Seule la version passe par -ldflags. Le commit et la date viennent des
# métadonnées que `-buildvcs=auto` embarque tout seul, et que
# `internal/version` lit en repli : les poser ici aussi serait une seconde
# source pour une réponse que le compilateur donne déjà. `git describe` sans
# `--always` échoue tant qu'aucun tag n'existe, et c'est voulu — un SHA promu
# au rang de numéro de version est pire que "dev".
shell = "bash -c"
run = '''
version=$(git describe --tags --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
go build -ldflags "-X github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/version.version=$version" -o "bin/dk$(go env GOEXE)" .
'''

[tasks.run]
description = "Build and run the application"
depends = ["build"]
shell = "bash -c"
run = './bin/dk$(go env GOEXE)'

[tasks.dev]
description = "Run directly with go run (faster for development)"
run = "go run ."

[tasks.setup]
description = "Run the `dk setup` context wizard directly with go run"
run = "go run . setup"

[tasks.test]
description = "Run all tests"
run = "go test -v ./..."

[tasks.test-race]
description = "Run tests with race detector (requires a C toolchain: gcc/clang)"
env = { CGO_ENABLED = "1" }
run = "go test -race ./..."

[tasks.cover]
description = "Run tests and report coverage per package"
run = "go test -cover ./..."

[tasks.fmt]
description = "Format code"
run = "go fmt ./..."

[tasks.fmt-check]
description = "Fail when a file is not gofmt-clean (fmt rewrites, this one reports)"
shell = "bash -c"
run = """
unformatted=$(gofmt -l .)
if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then
  echo "not gofmt-clean:"
  echo "$unformatted"
  exit 1
fi
"""

[tasks.vet]
description = "Run go vet"
run = "go vet ./..."

[tasks.lint]
description = "Run golangci-lint"
run = "golangci-lint run"

[tasks.tidy]
description = "Tidy dependencies"
run = "go mod tidy"

[tasks.deps]
description = "Download dependencies"
run = "go mod download"

[tasks.clean]
description = "Clean build artifacts"
shell = "bash -c"
run = """
rm -rf bin
go clean
"""

[tasks.install]
description = "Install the dk binary to $GOPATH/bin"
# Two things a bare `go install` gets wrong here. It names the binary after the

systemPrompt:
Tu développes DevDesk, un TUI DevSecOps local.

- Stack : Go 1.27.3 (`go.mod`), Bubble Tea, bubbles, lipgloss, client GitLab/GitHub, YAML (`gopkg.in/yaml.v3`)
- Architecture et dossiers clés : `internal/ui/<vue>` (une vue Bubble Tea par zone), `internal/ui/theme` (couleurs et styles), `internal/ui/keymap` (vocabulaire des touches), `internal/ui/datatable`, `internal/ui/components` (`FooterMessage`, `FilterBar`), `internal/app` (routeur), `internal/forge`, `internal/scan`, `internal/docker`, `internal/oci`, `internal/status`, `internal/config`, `internal/credentials`. Notes détaillées par zone dans `docs/architecture/*.md` (app-shell, configuration, forge, workspaces, filebrowser, viewer, scanning, registries, network, mcp, templates, ui-components) ; règles TUI dans `.claude/rules/*.md`.
- Commandes : build `mise run build` (ou `go build ./...`), lint `mise run lint` (golangci-lint, obligatoire avant commit), tests `mise run test` ; en plus `mise run test-race` (exige cgo et gcc/clang) et `mise run check` (fmt + vet + lint + test)
- Conventions spécifiques :
  - Commentaires de code et messages de commit en anglais (Rule 307), commits conventionnels ; texte d'interface et logs en anglais US (Rule 129).
  - Les touches viennent du vocabulaire `internal/ui/keymap` : actions en majuscule, lettres minuscules = filtres locaux déclarés dans `keymap.localToggles`, aucune lettre nue ne navigue (`TestNoBareLetterIsNavigation`).
  - Couleurs uniquement via `internal/ui/theme` (Rules 102, 119) ; fonds via `theme.Bg`, `PadWithBg`, `EmptyLineBg` (Rule 115/117).
  - Un case d'`Update()` de plus de 5 lignes s'extrait en `handle[Msg]()` (Rule 201).
  - Travail dans un worktree sous `.worktrees/<branche>` depuis `origin/main`, jamais de push sur `main` ; PR avec `gh -R anthnel/devdesk`.
  - Mettre à jour `docs/architecture/<zone>.md` dans le même commit que le code, et `GetHelpContent()` quand une touche change (Rule 114).
- Pièges connus :
  - Rule 110 : ne jamais modifier le modèle dans un `Cmd` ; seul `Update()` mute, le `Cmd` renvoie un message.
  - Rule 122 : `Cell` renvoie du texte brut sans séquence ANSI ; la couleur passe par `Style` (sinon troncature au milieu d'une séquence qui déborde sur les lignes suivantes). Pas de `style.Render()` dans `table.Row`.
  - Rule 128 : tout message de pied de page passe par `components.FooterMessage` (Error/Warn/Info, avec son timer retourné par `Update()`), jamais de style local.
  - Rule 130 : un raccourci sans objet est grisé (`Disabled`), pas retiré ; une seule `Availability` lue par l'en-tête et par le handler, refus explicite au footer.
  - Rule 139 : le corps d'une `datatable` est toujours `m.table.View()`, jamais un spinner ni un message.
  - Chaque colonne déclare son `Sizing` ; pas de `textarea` (utiliser `components.WrappedInput`) ; pas de touche `Tab` pour naviguer entre champs d'un formulaire (Rule 135).
  - `shared.State.Secrets` : une seule `Selection` par contexte, ne pas rappeler `credentials.Select()`.
  - `~/.devdesk/`, le keyring, Docker et les ports sont partagés entre worktrees.

Mêmes règles que l'agent `coder` : diffs minimaux, code qui ressemble au code voisin,
build, lint et tests lancés avant de rendre la main, pas de commit.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

# Most tasks are a single `go ...` invocation and run unchanged under both the
# POSIX shell and the "cmd /c" that mise defaults to on Windows. Tasks relying on
# POSIX syntax declare `shell = "bash -c"` explicitly — the global
# `windows_default_inline_shell_args` setting is refused from a project config.

[tools]
go = "1.27"
# Pinned so CI and every machine lint against the same rules. Without a pin, two
# golangci-lint versions disagree on what Rule 305 considers a clean run.
# 2.15.0 is the first line built with Go 1.27 (2.12.2 was built with go1.26 and
# refuses a go.mod that targets 1.27: "Go language version used to build
# golangci-lint is lower than the targeted Go version").
golangci-lint = "2.15.0"
# Pinned for the same reason, and it matters more here: goreleaser's own
# configuration schema changes between minor versions, so an unpinned tool
# would fail on `version: 2` syntax that was valid when it was written.
goreleaser = "2.18.0"
# Pinned for the same reason as the two above. Used by docs-serve/docs-build
# to run mkdocs-material without installing it as a mise tool: mkdocs-material
# is a theme/plugin package, not an app — it exposes no console-script entry
# point of its own (only its dependency `mkdocs` does), so `pipx:mkdocs-material`
# fails on every platform with "No executables are provided by package
# `mkdocs-material`". `uv tool run --with` sidesteps this by running `mkdocs`
# (which has an entry point) in an ephemeral environment with mkdocs-material
# injected alongside it.
uv = "0.12.10"

[tasks.build]
description = "Build the binary to bin/dk"
# `$(go env GOEXE)` for the same reason as [tasks.install]: `-o` takes the name
# literally, and PowerShell refuses to run an extension-less file even by
# explicit path — "Cannot run a document in the middle of a pipeline". Only
# `mise run run` uses this binary today, and it goes through bash, which is why
# nothing has complained. Empty on every other platform.
#
# Seule la version passe par -ldflags. Le commit et la date viennent des
# métadonnées que `-buildvcs=auto` embarque tout seul, et que
# `internal/version` lit en repli : les poser ici aussi serait une seconde
# source pour une réponse que le compilateur donne déjà. `git describe` sans
# `--always` échoue tant qu'aucun tag n'existe, et c'est voulu — un SHA promu
# au rang de numéro de version est pire que "dev".
shell = "bash -c"
run = '''
version=$(git describe --tags --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
go build -ldflags "-X github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/version.version=$version" -o "bin/dk$(go env GOEXE)" .
'''

[tasks.run]
description = "Build and run the application"
depends = ["build"]
shell = "bash -c"
run = './bin/dk$(go env GOEXE)'

[tasks.dev]
description = "Run directly with go run (faster for development)"
run = "go run ."

[tasks.setup]
description = "Run the `dk setup` context wizard directly with go run"
run = "go run . setup"

[tasks.test]
description = "Run all tests"
run = "go test -v ./..."

[tasks.test-race]
description = "Run tests with race detector (requires a C toolchain: gcc/clang)"
env = { CGO_ENABLED = "1" }
run = "go test -race ./..."

[tasks.cover]
description = "Run tests and report coverage per package"
run = "go test -cover ./..."

[tasks.fmt]
description = "Format code"
run = "go fmt ./..."

[tasks.fmt-check]
description = "Fail when a file is not gofmt-clean (fmt rewrites, this one reports)"
shell = "bash -c"
run = """
unformatted=$(gofmt -l .)
if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then
  echo "not gofmt-clean:"
  echo "$unformatted"
  exit 1
fi
"""

[tasks.vet]
description = "Run go vet"
run = "go vet ./..."

[tasks.lint]
description = "Run golangci-lint"
run = "golangci-lint run"

[tasks.tidy]
description = "Tidy dependencies"
run = "go mod tidy"

[tasks.deps]
description = "Download dependencies"
run = "go mod download"

[tasks.clean]
description = "Clean build artifacts"
shell = "bash -c"
run = """
rm -rf bin
go clean
"""

[tasks.install]
description = "Install the dk binary to $GOPATH/bin"
# Two things a bare `go install` gets wrong here. It names the binary after the
# module (`devdesk`), while the command — and `mise run build` — is `dk`; and
# mise's go plugin exports GOBIN=<mise>/installs/go/<version>/bin, so the binary
# would land in a directory that disappears on the next toolchain bump.
#
# `go env GOEXE` is what `go install` would have appended, and dropping it is not
# cosmetic on Windows: `-o` takes the name literally, so the file lands as `dk`
# with no extension. It is a valid PE and runs by explicit path — which is why
# `mise run run` never noticed — but PowerShell and cmd resolve a bare command
# through PATHEXT, so `dk` is simply not found. GOEXE is empty everywhere else.
#
# The destination is printed rather than tested. Whether `dk` will resolve is a
# question about the *calling* shell's PATH, and this task runs under bash: a
# check here would answer for the wrong shell and be believed. Saying where the
# binary went lets the reader answer it themselves, which is the one thing a
# "command not found" a second later does not tell them.
shell = "bash -c"
run = """
target="$(go env GOPATH)/bin/dk$(go env GOEXE)"
version=$(git describe --tags --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)

description = "Validate .goreleaser.yaml without building anything"
run = "goreleaser check"

[tasks.release]
description = "Build the release artifacts and attach them to the GitHub Release (CI only)"
# Needs GITHUB_TOKEN and a tag; it is the release workflow's build step, and
# running it by hand would publish. `release-snapshot` is the local equivalent.
run = "goreleaser release --clean"

[tasks.release-snapshot]
description = "Build the release artifacts locally, publishing nothing"
# `--snapshot` is what makes this runnable without a tag: goreleaser invents a
# version rather than refusing. It is the only way to find out that a build
# target is broken before a tag has been pushed, which is the point at which
# the mistake is expensive.
run = "goreleaser release --snapshot --clean"

[tasks.check]
description = "Run fmt, vet, lint and tests (pre-commit checklist)"
depends = ["fmt", "vet", "lint", "test"]

[tasks.docs-serve]
description = "Preview the documentation site locally"
shell = "bash -c"
# Same changelog staging step as docs-build — without it, mkdocs.yml's nav
# points at a changelog.md that doesn't exist yet on a fresh checkout.
run = """
cp CHANGELOG.md docs-site/docs/changelog.md
uv tool run --with mkdocs-material==9.6.14 mkdocs serve -f docs-site/mkdocs.yml
"""

description = "Build the static documentation site into docs-site/site"
shell = "bash -c"
# CHANGELOG.md is copied in rather than symlinked so the build works the same
# way locally and in CI, on every OS mise supports.
# --site-dir is resolved relative to the config file (-f), not the cwd: passing
# "docs-site/site" here built into docs-site/docs-site/site instead, so
# actions/upload-pages-artifact found nothing at docs-site/site in CI.
run = """
cp CHANGELOG.md docs-site/docs/changelog.md
uv tool run --with mkdocs-material==9.6.14 mkdocs build -f docs-site/mkdocs.yml --site-dir site
"""

description = "Write the ccusage reference file for internal/agentusage/crosscheck_test.go: mise run agentusage-ref -- <uuid>... > /path/outside/repo/ref.json (output outside the repo, never committed)"
# POSIX shell, npx and jq required, hence no Windows support. ccusage is pinned
# so the reference does not move under us. Its per-session JSON has a flat
# `totalTokens` plus an `entries` array carrying inputTokens, outputTokens,
# cacheReadTokens and cacheCreationTokens; ccusage's totalTokens is the sum of
# the four, which is what the crosscheck compares against. Only stdout is the
# reference: ccusage progress noise stays on stderr.
shell = "bash -c"
# mise appends trailing arguments to the script text rather than binding them to
# "$@", so the ids are declared with a usage spec and read from usage_ids.
usage = 'arg "<ids>" var=#true'
run = '''
set -euo pipefail
for id in $usage_ids; do
  npx --yes ccusage@20.0.43 claude session --id "$id" --json
done | jq -s '{sessions: map({
  id: .sessionId,
  total: .totalTokens,
  input: ([.entries[].inputTokens] | add // 0),
  output: ([.entries[].outputTokens] | add // 0),
  cacheRead: ([.entries[].cacheReadTokens] | add // 0),
  cacheWrite: ([.entries[].cacheCreationTokens] | add // 0)
})}'
'''

The page doesn't cover how to define checks in a Go module. It has no annotation syntax, no function signature, and no `dagger.json` or `.dagger` directory details. It does cover running and filtering checks.

**Listing checks**

```
dagger check -l
dagger check -l --all
dagger check -l --all --format=cli --go-package=store
```

The page says `-l` lists checks, `--all` expands collections to one row per item, and `--format=cli` prints the flags that select each row.

**Running and filtering checks**

```
dagger check
dagger check --go
dagger check --check=lint
dagger check --go --check=test
dagger check --go-package=store --go-test=TestFixture
```

**Stopping on first failure**

```
dagger check --fail-fast
```

By default, every check runs so you see all failures at once. `--fail-fast` cancels the remaining checks when one fails.

**Generated-file checks**

```
dagger check --generated=false
```

Generated-file checks run by default. This flag skips them and overrides the workspace's `check-generated` setting.

**Selecting a Git workspace**

```
dagger check github.com/dagger/dagger@main:golang
```

content.content:
The page doesn't cover `dagger init` or `dagger install`, so I can't give exact commands for those. It does describe how to wire modules through `dagger.toml`.

**1. Declare the modules in `dagger.toml`**

Each installed module gets a `[modules.<name>]` section with a `source`. Your app module and the module you're wiring into both need one:

```toml
[modules.myapp]
source = "./ci/myapp"

[modules.playwright]
source = "dagger.io/js/playwright"
```

**2. Add a settings entry that points to a function**

Under `[modules.<name>.settings]`, set the constructor argument to a `dag://<module>/<function>` address. The page's example wires a service:

```toml
[modules.playwright.settings]
service = "dag://myapp/serve"
```

The same pattern works for containers, files, directories, and workspaces, for example `baseCtr = "dag://base-images/chromium"`.

**3. Find wirable functions**

Run `dagger list services` to see every service in the workspace and the module that provides it. For other artifact types, the page says `dagger list` shows artifacts by type.

**4. Run it**

Run `dagger check --playwright`. Dagger resolves the reference when it builds the playwright module and passes in the running service.

**Notes**

- For the workspace main module, drop the module segment, as in `dag://serve`. The `dagger module settings` command can write the full address for you.
- A value with `dag://` must resolve. A missing function or type mismatch is a hard error, not a fallback. Values without `dag://`, such as `alpine:3.20`, keep their ordinary meaning.
- To pass a reference on the command line, use it as a flag: `dagger api call playwright --service=dag://myapp/serve ...`.

Under `[modules.<name>.settings]`, set the constructor argument to a `dag://<module>/<function>` address. The page's example wires a service:

```toml
[modules.playwright.settings]
service = "dag://myapp/serve"
```

The same pattern works for containers, files, directories, and workspaces, for example `baseCtr = "dag://base-images/chromium"`.

**3. Find wirable functions**

Run `dagger list services` to see every service in the workspace and the module that provides it. For other artifact types, the page says `dagger list` shows artifacts by type.

**4. Run it**

Run `dagger check --playwright`. Dagger resolves the reference when it builds the playwright module and passes in the running service.

**Notes**

- For the workspace main module, drop the module segment, as in `dag://serve`. The `dagger module settings` command can write the full address for you.
- A value with `dag://` must resolve. A missing function or type mismatch is a hard error, not a fallback. Values without `dag://`, such as `alpine:3.20`, keep their ordinary meaning.
- To pass a reference on the command line, use it as a flag: `dagger api call playwright --service=dag://myapp/serve ...`.

The search turned up the 1.0-beta Go SDK docs, but none of the results show the `+check` annotation syntax itself. The Go page only points to a separate "Checks, generators, services, directives" page for that.

- **Checks are workspace-level.** The 1.0-beta checks guide describes a check as a function that validates the caller's project, not the module's own code. It takes no required arguments, so it can run locally, in CI, or in Cloud. Checks validate the caller's project. SDK tests validate the module implementation.
- **Scaffolding a module.** The 1.0-beta Go SDK page says you install the SDK into the workspace, then run `dagger module init go my-module` from inside a Git repo. That command writes `dagger-module.toml` and `main.go`, updates the workspace config, and runs the generator.
- **Config layout.** In the 1.0-beta page, `dagger-module.toml` holds the module name, the engine version (v1.0.0-beta.11 in the example), and a `[runtime]` section with `source = "go"`. The workspace `dagger.toml` separately records the module under `modules.dagger-go-sdk.as-sdk`, which is how binding generation finds workspace modules.
- **Older layout.** Some pages (the `next` Go SDK docs, targeting engine v0.21.0) still describe a `dagger.json` with `sdk.source: "go"` and `dagger -m github.com/dagger/go-sdk call init`. Treat that as a different generation of the tooling, not the 1.0-beta layout.
- **Official Go module.** The Go module, `dagger/go`, runs checks across a workspace. It provides `go:test-all` and `go:lint-all`, and a module is excluded by adding a `!`-prefixed path to the selector array.

Next step: the exact `+check` annotation syntax is probably on the 1.0-beta "Checks, generators, services, directives, and ignore patterns" page. I'd fetch that page directly to confirm the syntax.

I can't reproduce the page verbatim, because the rules limit quotes to 125 characters. Here are the key points, with short excerpts.

**Install the Go SDK into your workspace (once):**

```
dagger module install dagger.io/sdk/go
```

If the repository has no `dagger.toml` yet, the page suggests `dagger module install --here dagger.io/sdk/go`. Run these from inside a Git repository.

**Create a module:**

```
dagger module init go --name my-module
```

This returns a changeset for you to review before anything is written to disk. By default, the module is created beside the `dagger.toml` being edited, under `.dagger/modules/<name>`. The `--path` flag chooses a different location.

**Resulting files:**

- `dagger-module.toml` holds the module name, the required `engineVersion`, and a `[runtime]` section. That section sets `source = "go"`, which tells the engine to use the Go runtime.
- `main.go` is your code. It's a `package main` file with a main object struct named after the module, such as `MyModule`. Each exported method becomes a callable Dagger Function.
- Generated files include `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `dagger.gen.go`, and `internal/dagger/`. Commit them, and don't edit them by hand.

**Checks with the `+check` pragma:** Put `// +check` in the doc comment of a method that returns only an `error`. The page's example is a `Lint` method on `MyModule`. Its signature begins with `func (m *MyModule) Lint(ctx context.Context) error`. The function runs a container with `Sync` and returns the error, so a non-zero exit fails the check. Run all checks with `dagger check`.

**Links to related sections:**

- Checks, generators, services, and ignore patterns: [Checks, generators, services, directives, and ignore patterns](https://docs.dagger.io/reference/sdks/go#checks-generators-services-directives-and-ignore-patterns)
- Magic comment directives table: [Magic comment directives](https://docs.dagger.io/reference/sdks/go#magic-comment-directives)
- Checks section: [Checks](https://docs.dagger.io/reference/sdks/go#checks)
- Running checks: [Checking your code](https://docs.dagger.io/using/checking)

This page has no separate checks or directives page. Those topics are sections within the Go SDK reference.

toolu_01ETSbbfweqL3YAUfYzJthaV.prompt: Section 'Checks, generators, services, directives, and ignore patterns' and the Workspace type: how a module function accesses the project directory (dagger.Workspace? +defaultPath? +ignore?), with short code examples, and magic comment directives table.

content.content:
The page doesn't mention `+defaultPath` or `+ignore`. Module functions instead get the project through a `*dagger.Workspace` argument, and ignore rules go on the directory read.

**Accessing the project directory**

Declare a `*dagger.Workspace` argument on the constructor or a function. Dagger "auto-populates it from the current workspace," and you don't pass it on the CLI. Content loads lazily, when a function reads a path:

```go
func New(ws *dagger.Workspace) *MyModule {
	return &MyModule{
		Source: ws.Directory("/"), // nothing is uploaded until used
	}
}
```

The `Workspace` type provides these accessors:

- `ws.Directory(path, opts...)` returns a `*dagger.Directory`.
- `ws.File(path)` returns a `*dagger.File`.
- `ws.FindUp(ctx, name, opts...)` returns the workspace path of the nearest match, searching upward.

A relative path resolves from the workspace's current directory. An absolute path (starting with `/`) resolves from the workspace root.

**Ignore patterns**

Filtering uses the `dagger.WorkspaceDirectoryOpts` struct, not a directive:

```go
Source: ws.Directory("/", dagger.WorkspaceDirectoryOpts{
	Exclude: []string{"node_modules", ".git", "dist"},
	// Include:   []string{"app/", "package.*"}, // allowlist instead
	// Gitignore: true,                          // apply .gitignore rules
}),
```

The page notes that tighter filters improve cache efficiency because less content loads, which means fewer invalidations.

**Checks, generators, and services**

- `// +check` on a method that returns `error` makes it a check run by `dagger check`.
- `// +generate` on a method that returns `*dagger.Changeset` makes it a generator run by `dagger generate`.
- A method returning `*dagger.Service` with no required arguments is a service run by `dagger start`. It needs no pragma.

**Magic comment directives**

| Directive | Placement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `// +optional` | argument | argument is optional |
| `// +default="x"` | argument | optional, with a default value |
| `// +private` | struct field | keeps the field out of the API |
| `// +check` | method | marks a check |
| `// +generate` | method | marks a generator |
| `// +collection` | struct | marks a collection type |
| `// +keys` | struct field | the collection's keys |
| `// +get` | method | returns one collection item |
| `// +delta` | struct field | receives changes to a collection's keys |

DEVDESK-343 spike S1: verdict is feasible on Windows with Docker Desktop, with friction that is not blocking. Worktree: C:\Users\anthoni\projects\entire\anthnel\devdesk\.worktrees\spike-dagger, branch spike/dagger, commit 2aa0cf75 (local only, nothing pushed, main untouched).

Setup
- Version: dagger v1.0.0-beta.27 (commit 400b82d6), which is a 1.0 beta, so nothing to reinstall. I did not time the Dagger install, since dagger.exe was already there.
- Engine: Docker Desktop 29.9.2, container dagger-engine-v1.0.0-beta.27 (registry.dagger.io/engine:v1.0.0-beta.27).
- The engine's first start took about 38 s (engine image pull plus workspace init), which fits the earlier 120 s hang.
- No skill named git-worktree-pr was found on disk, so I created the worktree by hand from origin/main.

Criteria
1. OK. `dagger check -l` lists exactly 6: build, fmt-check, lint, test, test-race, vet. Dagger adds a 7th check, go-sdk:stale (staleness of generated code). I removed it with `check-generated = false` in dagger.toml; `--generated=false` also works.
2. OK. Cold `dagger check` (the very first run to complete) took 6m26s and all six checks were green. The tests ran as uid 1000 (`id -u` = 1000).
   - Skipped tests: 4 with `go test -json`.
     - jobs/TestTargetKeyCleansWindowsPaths
     - agentusage/TestSessionTotalsMatchCcusage
     - oci_resources: a_form_replaces_the_table subtest
     - app/TestMeasureRedrawCost
   - Gap against the reference: the 3 agentusage root skips are gone because the user is non-root. The 9 no-git skips are gone because git is installed in the image. The 4 above are Windows-only or opt-in tests that I did not look into further.
   - The exit code under `dagger check` itself was not captured from bash; every captured exit code is 0 on success and 1 on failure.
3. OK. test-race passes, run through `mise run test-race` (CGO_ENABLED=1 comes from mise.toml). gcc and libc6-dev come from apt in the image.
4. OK. I added a failing test in the repo root package and reverted it afterwards. Exit code 1, `ci/test` is named as ERROR, and test-race failed too. All six checks are reported (the independent ones finished OK) and the full test output is shown. `dagger check --fail-fast` exists and cancels the remaining checks on the first failure. `-j/--parallel N` caps concurrency.
5. Partial.
   - Exclusions: the module excludes .worktrees, bin, .dagger and .git via `ws.Directory("/", Exclude)`. The upload was about 11 MB.
   - Caches: cache volumes are mounted for GOMODCACHE, GOCACHE and the mise data directory.
   - .git: in a worktree it is a file (`gitdir: C:/...`), which is useless in the container. The workspace API did not expose it to the container.
   - `git describe` fails there ("not a git repository"), so the build task takes its `|| echo dev` branch and the version is "dev". `go build` still succeeds, because Go only embeds VCS metadata when it finds a .git. The task build is green. A cold dagger check run does not carry the real version or commit.
6. OK. The module has no Go or golangci-lint version literal; mise reads them from mise.toml. The only pins are mise v2026.10.18 and the debian:bookworm-slim digest sha256:734a72b3.... Two other places mention a version and are not hand-written pins: the generated `go 1.27` in .dagger/modules/ci/go.mod and the generated dagger.io SDK beta.25 dependency. Divergence consigned: mise.toml says go = "1.27", go.mod says 1.27.3, and mise resolves the latest 1.27.x (the host has 1.27.4). The container may therefore differ from the 1.27.3 floor in go.mod, and nothing checks it.
7. OK. The hand-written module is 82 lines (.dagger/modules/ci/main.go). The generated files come on top. That includes the `Skips` measurement helper, 3 lines, which I left in.

Timings
- Cold run: 6m26s (apt, mise install, and test at 5m58s, test-race at 6m24s).
- Warm run with identical source: 1.6 s, everything served from the engine cache.
- Warm run after a source change: build 1.8 s, vet 1.2 s, lint 5.6 s, fmt-check 0.6 s. test ran 4m42 and test-race 4m58 (broken-test run, all fail). The Go caches are mounted but test is still about 5 minutes with a one-file change, so this suite is slow or its results are not cacheable.
- With a changed source, the total was 5 min (300 s).

Frictions
- Bash tool: dagger.exe hung even on `--help`, but ran in 0.1 s from PowerShell with redirected output. Probably a stdin/TTY quirk of Git Bash, not an engine problem; the hang was not (only) the engine's first start. I drove it through PowerShell, which also has script execution disabled.
- Authoring a Go module needs `dagger module install --here dagger.io/sdk/go` then `dagger module init go --name ci`. After any API change, run `dagger generate -y`, otherwise `check -l` and `call` show stale functions. The template main.go uses a non-standard `core.NewContainer()`, and the docs fetched through WebFetch were incomplete (I got the Go page and the checks page, not `+check` examples elsewhere).
- Cache volumes mount root-owned parent directories, which made mise fail with a permission error. I pre-created and chowned the directories in the image.
- Concurrent checks share the mise cache; `mise install` is a single deduplicated step in the base container, so there was no race.
- Output encoding on Windows is garbled in a PowerShell redirect (UTF-16 and mojibake).

Open points
- The Dagger exit code under cmd/PowerShell was not checked outside my wrapper.
- 4 skips are unexplained beyond the names above.
- Real version/commit marking in the container would need the `.git` content, which is not available from a worktree.
- The arm64 case (the mise download URL is hardcoded to linux-x64) was not tested.
- The ~5 min test time in the container versus on the host was not compared.

DEVDESK-344 (S2): Dagger is faster than `mise run ci` on every comparison, and the <= 1.2 criterion is met (hot ratio 0.73). Both tools hit the same wall, though: `mise run ci` on Windows fails at `test`, so it never reaches `test-race`. Nothing was pushed and main is untouched. All timings are wall-clock seconds from a PowerShell wrapper, same machine, run sequentially.

**Setup**
- Eval worktree: C:\Users\anthoni\projects\entire\anthnel\devdesk\.worktrees\spike-dagger-eval, detached at each commit. Logs and scripts: C:\Users\anthoni\spike-s2\ (results.txt, run.ps1, seq*.ps1).
- Overlay on each commit: .dagger/, dagger.toml and dagger.lock from spike/dagger (module commit 2aa0cf75, unchanged), plus the [tasks.ci] block from origin/main:mise.toml (d5e7e85d). The commits predate that task, so I appended it to both sides.
- Failing commit: branch spike/dagger-fail, commit a70bc1c0, based on 2f383dec with zz_spike_test.go (a failing test). Throwaway, not pushed.
- Chosen commit for the 3 measures: 2f383dec.
- GitHub verdicts, from `gh run view --json jobs`: all 6 steps are success on 9c6c7825, 2f383dec, 5f76cc16 and 56166bf8. The Test job runs `mise run test` then `test-race`. Per-step durations are not detailed, so I did not use them.

**1. Verdicts**

| commit | fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race: Dagger | GitHub | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 56166bf8, 5f76cc16, 2f383dec, 9c6c7825 | all 6 OK | all 6 success | none |
| spike/dagger-fail | test ERROR, test-race ERROR, other 4 OK | not run; deduced: `test` fails and the Test job stops, so `test-race` is skipped | `test-race` red on Dagger |

- The `test-race` gap on the failing commit is explained. Dagger runs the checks independently, and the broken test is in a package that `test-race` also runs.
- Cold run on 2f383dec was green on Dagger too.

**2. Durations in seconds (hot = after a code change, never a rerun of the same commit)**

| | Dagger | mise run ci |
|---|---|---|
| Cold on 2f383dec, total | 413 (build 75, fmt 32, lint 87, vet 75, test 360, test-race 387, in parallel) | 504, exit 1 (vet 25, lint 13, build 11, fmt 0.2, test about 454 and failing) |
| Hot 2f383dec, 3 runs | 298.6 / 298.7 / 298.7, median 298.7, exit 0 | 424.7 / 410.5 / 407.6, median 410.5, exit 1 |
| Hot 56166bf8 | 317.6 | 422.5 |
| Hot 5f76cc16 | 317.1 | 423.1 |
| Hot 9c6c7825 | 305.4 | 418.5 |

- Hot per-check on 2f383dec, Dagger: fmt 0.7, vet 1.3, lint 5.2, build 2.0, test 281, test-race 297.
- Hot per-check on 2f383dec, mise: fmt 0.2, vet 1.0, lint 1.9, build 1.2, then test, which fails.
- For the 3 hot repeats I appended a unique stamp line to main.go. Without it, the Dagger engine memoizes an identical source and replied in 1.8 s; I discarded those runs. Earlier mise repeats without a stamp were within 4 s of the stamped ones.
- Cold: the Dagger engine container and its volume were removed, `go clean -cache -modcache` was run and the golangci-lint cache cleaned. `go clean` could not delete 3 files because a devdesk.exe belonging to you was running; I did not touch it.
- Cold, Dagger: the engine image stayed (not part of the authorized wipe), so the cold figure includes the apt, mise and tool installs but not the engine image pull.

**3. Ratio**
- Hot ratio, Dagger / mise, median of 3: 298.7 / 410.5 = 0.73. Criterion (<= 1.2) met.
- The CI GitHub reference of 322 s is also above Dagger's 298.7.
- `mise run ci` on Windows never reaches `test-race`: `test` fails first. The host has a C compiler (scoop mingw gcc), so the premise "no gcc" is wrong. `mise run test-race` alone starts and runs with CGO_ENABLED=1. It fails on the same Windows tests, and I did not time it to the end.
- `test` fails on Windows for reasons unrelated to this spike: path separators and file-name rules in agentusage, app, config, engine, imageupdate, jobs and others. `mise run ci` is therefore red on a clean commit on this machine; only the first red test matters in the table above.
- Excluding `test-race`, hot on 2f383dec: Dagger `--skip test-race` 282.4 against mise 410.5, ratio 0.69 (mise never ran `test-race`).
- `test-race` alone on Dagger, hot: 295.9 s, passes, usable. In the full parallel run it takes 297 s.

**4. Failing commit**
- Time to first failure: Dagger `check` fails at 301.8 s (test 283, test-race 299). `--fail-fast` brought it to 284.2 s, and it still reports both `test` and `test-race` as ERROR. mise run ci fails at 424.6 s.
- Which output localizes the failure faster: Dagger, with a summary naming `test` and the failing test `TestSpikeBroken` (at about 283 s, against about 425 s for mise).
- On Windows, mise shows the broken test at line 31 of a long scroll mixed with dozens of unrelated Windows failures.
- `--fail-fast` brings little here, because both failing checks end at the same moment.

**5. Why `test` takes about 5 min in the container**
- It is not CPU contention: `--check=test` alone takes 280 s, against 281 s inside the full parallel run.
- It is not the Go cache being lost: I changed only main.go (stamp runs) and `test` still takes 281 s.
- The host is just as slow, if not slower: internal/app alone took 409 s on the host.
- Not verified: I suspect the tests of internal/app (and agentusage at 142 s on the host) are heavy or never cache, for example through environment changes in tests. I did not isolate the cause.

**Frictions**
- `--skip` and `--check` work as expected. `dagger check` output is UTF-16 and mojibake when redirected from PowerShell.
- A Dagger run of the same source returns in 1.8 s from the engine cache. That is valid for CI reruns but not for the hot measure.
- Windows tests fail, so the local reference for the `mise run ci` side can only be a Linux GitHub run.
- The module still has no real VCS version in the container (.git absent), as in S1.

**Open points**
- Why the tests are slow and whether they can be cached (`internal/app`).
- Cold Dagger without the engine image pull was not measured.
- The GitHub rate on this machine was not compared against the host runner.
- If `mise run ci` should also pass on Windows, the failing tests need fixing first.
